parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the focal length of a converging lens. Refer to Fig. 3.1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Set up the apparatus as shown in Fig. 3.1.

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Measure the height h O of the illuminated object. Fig. 3.1 shows the height to measure on the illuminated object provided. h O = ................................................... cm [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Place the lens a distance u = 20.0 cm from the illuminated object. Place the screen near the lens. Switch on the lamp. Move the screen until a focused image of the illuminated object is seen on the screen. Measure, and record in Table 3.1, the height h I of the image on the screen. Repeat the procedure for u = 25.0 cm, 30.0 cm, 35.0 cm and 40.0 cm. Switch off the lamp. Table 3.1 u / cm h I / cm W 20.0 25.0 30.0 35.0 40.0 [1]

ms.label: 3(a)(iii)
ms.text: move screen slowly / back and forth

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) For each distance u , calculate, and record in Table 3.1, a value W . Use your results from (a) and the equation W = h O h I . [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Plot a graph of u / cm ( y -axis) against W ( x -axis). You do not need to start your axes at the origin (0, 0). Draw the best-fit line. [4]

ms.label: 3(c)
ms.text:
graph:

axes labelled with quantity and unit

appropriate scales (plots occupying at least ½ grid between plotted points)

plots all correct to ½ small square and precise plots

well-judged line and thin line

parts.label: i
parts.text: (d) (i) Determine the gradient G of the line. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(d)(i)
ms.text: G present and triangle method seen on graph

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The focal length f of the lens is numerically equal to the gradient G . Record a value of f for this experiment. f = ................................................... cm [1]

ms.label: 3(d)(ii)
ms.text: f in range 12.0 (cm) to 18.0 (cm) and to 2 or 3 significant figures

ms.label: 3(e)
ms.text: values of hI become (very) small / difficult to measure or greater % uncertainty
